_what: Estimated daily cost of clearing the supervised review queue, asked before recruiting because a supervision step that is too slow becomes rubber-stamping.

reply_length_chars._why_this_population: these are replies this system actually produced, so the reading cost is derived from real output length rather than an assumed one

edit_rate._why_this_is_a_LOWER_bound: A2 was measured on our own authored corpora, which share vocabulary and framing with our facts by construction (R21/R33). Real traffic is a different population and every time this project has measured one, the mechanism did worse on it — 1.9% vs 71% on the coverage gate, 42/42 OOC leaks across two axes.

_modelled_inputs._not_measured: seconds per decision is MODELLED, not measured. decision_latency_s is recorded on every item and review_summary() reports the median, so the pilot replaces this estimate with a real number inside the first week.

rows.note: ten employers, one question each per day — the quiet case
ten employers, two each — the planning case
ten employers, three each — a busy day, or the first week when the novelty is high
five employers, two each — the cohort that fits a 'few minutes a day' budget
three employers, two each — the cohort that fits comfortably

verdict.question_asked: does clearing it take more than a few minutes a day for ten users?
verdict._the_second_cost_no_estimate_captures: LATENCY, not minutes. A supervised answer cannot arrive faster than the reviewer, so a 9pm question waits until morning. That changes what the pilot MEASURES — a user who waits twelve hours for their first answer may simply stop asking, and the transcripts would then under-report demand rather than reveal it. The acks say a person is checking, which is honest, but honesty is not immediacy.
